headline.text: UN climate talks run into overtime over fossil fuels
headline.context: The latest draft deal no longer mentions them.
headline.vo: The UN climate summit in Turkey has run into overtime. Nearly two hundred countries are still negotiating in Antalya, split over whether the final deal should mention fossil fuels.

beats.text: COP31 was due to end on *Friday* evening
beats.vo: The talks, known as COP31, were due to end on Friday evening. Negotiators are still meeting on Saturday, and a new text is expected.

beats.title: How it unfolded
beats.vo: The summit opened on the ninth of November. On Thursday, a new draft removed all mentions of fossil fuels. On Friday, the deadline passed without an agreement. On Saturday, the talks went into overtime.

beats.quote: It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover document that does not even mention fossil fuels.
beats.vo: Panama, France and other countries want a clear transition away from fossil fuels. Turkey's environment minister, Murat Kurum, who presides over the summit, says they are close to the finish line, but not there yet.

title: UN climate talks COP31 run into overtime over fossil fuels
caption: The UN climate summit COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, has run into overtime after missing its Friday evening deadline. Nearly 200 countries are divided over a draft deal that no longer mentions fossil fuels. Panama, France and others are pushing for a clear transition away from coal, oil and gas. A new text is expected on Saturday.
